newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SGB SHARE SEEN SLIPPING ON TRACTEBEL BUY.
newsitem.headline: SGB SHARE SEEN SLIPPING ON TRACTEBEL BUY.

text.p: Shares in Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA were seen slipping on Wednesday on the back of news the company would pay 49 billion Belgian francs to buy out Groupe Bruxelles Lambert's 24.47 percent stake in utility group Tractebel .
"I'm not a trader but I think there's more likely to be downward rather than upward pressure on SGB's share," analyst Dirk Peeters of KB Securities told Reuters.
Peeters estimated SGB was paying 1.8 times Tractebel's book value, or goodwill of between 15 and 20 billion Belgian francs. "I don't know how the market will evaluate the price," he said.
SGB said on Tuesday it would finance its acquisition mainly from new loans as its cash was needed to subscribe to a capital increase at its Generale Bank unit.
SGB said it would also offer all Tractebel shareholders the chance to sell at 14,500 francs a share, the agreed price it is paying GBL units Electrafina and Royale Belge for their Tractebel shares.
SGB said it believed most private shareholders would not take up the offer because it would also issue them a free put warrant allowing them to sell at the same price in three years.
"They assume most people will not sell...but even if only 10 or 20 percent do they will have to come up with another 10 or 20 billion francs," Peeters noted.
